comparator: Joanot Valero dyer's manual as recovered and edited
mechanism_supported: Vernacular master-artisan Fachliteratur; dye recipes, stain removal, medical recipes, abbreviations, accounts and an older copied exemplar in one book.
limitation: The surviving evidence is a later microfilm of a lost manuscript and the mixed medical content prevents a purely nonmedical analogy.

comparator: Beinecke MS 1129 recipe book for colors
mechanism_supported: A German whole-volume craft recipe book makes plant/color batches, measures and local procedures a real manuscript genre.
limitation: About fifty years later than 1420 and not a bathhouse book.

comparator: Cambridge UL MS Ee.1.15 ink recipe presented by St Edmund Hall
mechanism_supported: Take, crush, pot, rainwater, stir and wait three days demonstrate ordinary concrete workshop recipe order near 1420.
limitation: Ink is only an analogy for plant/material batching, not a match to any unit.

comparator: Bologna Manuscript or Secrets of Colours
mechanism_supported: Late-medieval handbook for preparing paints establishes a practical recipe/exemplar environment.
limitation: Paint technology does not identify the five plant images.

date_and_region: fifteenth or sixteenth century Arabic copy
comparator: British Library Or 5927 craft treatise via Qatar Digital Library
mechanism_supported: One technical collection includes soap, fruit waters, stain removal, cloth dyes, verdigris, rosewater and scent materials.
limitation: Date is broad and cultural route to this codex is unproved.

comparator: CSIC study of perfume and cosmetic recipe books
mechanism_supported: About fifty recipes record ingredients, preparation techniques and applications, supporting scent-water and oil branches.
limitation: Medicine, body care and perfume overlap; this does not yield a clean nonmedical boundary.

mechanism_supported: Shows a near-period illustrated plant-to-water production scene labeled aqua rosata or rosenwaszer.
limitation: Rose rather than violet; the Tacuinum frame is health-related.

date_and_region: medieval Denmark with German and Swedish comparisons
mechanism_supported: Common sweat bath used heated stones, cold water on stones, birch switches and a cold rinse; staff could add haircutting, bleeding and wound care.
limitation: Bathhouse and medicine historically overlap, so the comparator supports both theories.

comparator: Roberta Magnusson, Water Technology in the Middle Ages
mechanism_supported: Sources, gradients, cisterns, branch pipes, conduit heads, tanks, drains, cleaning, repair and skilled work make the Bio operations technically real.
limitation: A general historical synthesis, not a direct match to these drawings.

mechanism_supported: A working mariner compiled vernacular mathematics, astronomy, astrology, navigation, shipbuilding and voyage records in one practical manuscript.
limitation: It supports technical-plus-Astro miscellany, but no herbal or 28-entry mapping.

comparator: Staatsbibliothek Berlin concertina calendar Libr. pict. A 92
mechanism_supported: Portable calendar combines saints, labors of months, zodiac and daylight wheels for practical time visualization.
limitation: Twelve monthly labors do not explain either 28-part diagram.

comparator: Morgan MS M.941 almanac and calendar
mechanism_supported: Folded calendar combines zodiac, thunder prognostications and occupations of months in a practical object.
limitation: Still includes a Vein Man and therefore cannot serve as a strictly nonmedical parallel.

date_and_region: 1150-1200 Germany; still acquired and annotated in the fifteenth century
mechanism_supported: One technical codex combines colors, arts, water finding, ointments, alchemy, glaze, parchment and ink; fifteenth-century owners added recipes and Nicholas of Cusa bought it in 1444.
limitation: The core is much earlier and includes medical matter; it proves miscellany survival, not V68 authorship.
